preamble: The transformation of a palatal glide [j] into a voiced palatal stop [ɟ] is a classic example of fortition, often occurring in environments where glides are strengthened at the beginning of a syllable or word. This process, also known as consonantalization, is seen in the historical development of Romance and in languages like Kirundi. In Albanian, word-initial *j (from PIE *y and from *s) hardened to gj [ɟ] (*jama > gjem 'bridle').

examples.note: Initial stage of palatal glide strengthening in Early Romance.
Regular strengthening of glides in certain phonological contexts.
Initial *j > dʲ; cf. Tundra Nenets яля
